label: Diagnostic centres
eyebrow: For diagnostic centres · sample to report
h1Parts: Reports the patient doesn’t call you about
lead: Diagnostic centres live and die by turnaround time and report-pickup. Lucoze is built around the sample lifecycle — collection, processing, signing, dispatch — with home-collection routing set up for your centre during onboarding.
why: Home-collection routing set up for your centre during onboarding, so the phlebotomist knows where to go and the front desk stops chasing by phone.
Barcode at collection and an audit trail through processing and signing, set up for your lab during onboarding.
Tests that go to a reference lab tracked alongside in-house — same patient view, same TAT.
Hospital + clinic referrals invoiced separately. Revenue split visible per partner per month.

detail.title: Built around the sample lifecycle
detail.body: A diagnostic centre is a pipeline: collection, processing, signing, dispatch. Lucoze tracks each sample through those stages with a barcode from the point of collection, so at any moment you know which samples are pending, which are with the pathologist, and which reports are ready. The patient is notified on dispatch instead of calling the front desk to chase a result.

detail.title: Home collection and reference labs, in one view
detail.body: Home-collection routing is set up for your centre during onboarding, and tests sent to an outside reference lab sit in the same patient view as in-house work. B2B referrals from hospitals and clinics are invoiced separately, with the revenue split visible per partner.

detail.title: From registration to report, every sample has a status
detail.body: A test moves through fixed steps: registration, sample collection, barcoding, processing, result entry, and report delivery. Lucoze records which step each barcoded sample is on, so when a patient or a referring doctor asks where a report is, the front desk answers from the screen instead of walking to the lab bench. Reference ranges and report layouts are set up for your lab during onboarding. Home-collection samples join this same chain the moment the phlebotomist marks them collected. Because each step is stamped with who did it and when, the same record answers a where-is-my-report question and supports the documentation a NABL-oriented lab keeps.

detail.title: Turnaround time you watch before the patient calls
detail.body: Every test has an expected turnaround, set up for your lab during onboarding. Lucoze records when the sample was collected, so the lab can see which samples are still pending and chase the delay before the patient rings to ask. The same view covers tests sent to an outside reference lab, so a send-out sits in the same place as in-house work rather than disappearing until the report comes back.

faqs.q: Does Lucoze support home sample collection?
faqs.a: Yes. Home-collection routing is set up for your centre during onboarding, and each sample is tracked from collection through to report dispatch.

faqs.q: Does the workflow support NABL documentation?
faqs.a: The barcode at collection and the audit trail through processing and signing support NABL documentation. Accreditation itself remains the lab's responsibility.
They appear alongside in-house tests in the same patient view and are tracked to the same turnaround, so nothing falls between systems.

faqs.q: Can staff tell a patient exactly where their sample is?
faqs.a: Yes. Each barcoded sample carries the step it is on — collected, in processing, result entered, or dispatched — so the front desk reads the current status off the screen rather than checking with the lab bench.

faqs.q: Does Lucoze show reference ranges on reports?
faqs.a: Reference ranges are set up for your lab during onboarding and appear on the report that reaches the referring doctor and the patient.
